name: tram
tagline: Test Runner for Assertion Manifests: develop, test and release

check.desc: Offline gate: unit tests, manifest corpus, assertion smoke test, command docs
check.detail:
Run it before every commit. It needs no network and no free port.

The command-docs part runs `justz check` and the `justz fmt` order check: it fails when a recipe and its entry in config/commands.json disagree. Run `justz fmt` to fix the order.

ci.desc: Full gate: check, packed-package test, then the Tasks API integration test on port 3000
ci.detail:
What the GitHub Actions test workflow runs. It adds the slow parts that `just check` leaves out: it packs the tarball into dist/ and installs it in a temporary project, then starts the Tasks sample API and runs its manifest.

Fails at once when port 3000 is in use; free it with `just sample stop`.

clean.desc: Delete dist/ and .tram/ (packed tarballs and sample evidence)

doctor.desc: Check node, npm, just, justz and the other tools a contributor needs
doctor.detail: Also reports whether port 3000 is free and whether the sample API dependencies are installed. Optional tools (gh, python3, shellcheck) only warn.

exits.1: a required tool is missing, or node is older than 18

help.desc: Full command reference, or the focused docs of one group or command (help [group] [term]); -b browses, -j emits JSON

link.desc: Link this checkout as the global tram command (npm link)
link.detail: After this, `tram` in any directory runs this checkout. Undo with `just unlink`. Not needed for `just run`.

run.desc: Run tram from this checkout; all args go to bin/tram (manifest first, then flags)
run.detail: Same CLI as the published `tram` command, run from source, so no `npm link` is needed. The target API must already be up: for a sample API, start it first with `just sample serve <name>` in another terminal.

args.name: -c, --validate
args.desc: Validate the manifest only; sends no HTTP requests

args.name: -r, --report <file>
args.desc: Write the JSON behavioral report to <file>

exits.0: every test passed, or the manifest is valid with -c
exits.1: a test failed, or a manifest or usage error

test.desc: Run the unit tests in test/*.test.js; extra args go to node --test

unlink.desc: Remove the global tram link made by just link
unlink.detail: Also removes a globally installed @mamund/tram from npm, if there is one instead of a link.

validate.desc: Validate one or more manifests without sending HTTP requests

exits.1: at least one manifest is invalid

check.desc: Validate every manifest in examples/ and api-samples/; must-fail manifests must be rejected
check.detail:
Must-fail manifests are examples/bad-manifests/*.json and examples/capture/bad-*.json. Files named *-report.json are TRAM output and are skipped. Sends no HTTP requests.

Put a new must-fail manifest in examples/bad-manifests/ so this check expects it to fail.

exits.1: a good manifest failed or a must-fail manifest passed

node-api.desc: Run the Node.js API example against a temporary Tasks server on port 3000
node-api.detail: Runs examples/node-api/run-tasks.cjs, which uses the public `loadManifest()` and `run()` API. Stops the server afterwards. Fails at once when port 3000 is in use.

smoke.desc: Run the assertion engine smoke test against fake responses (no HTTP)

release.label: npm package: pack, accept, version, tag, publish

accept.desc: Pack the tarball into dist/ and test it installed in a clean temporary project
accept.detail: Replaces dist/ on every run. The test installs the tarball with npm, then checks the installed CLI and the public Node.js API against a local HTTP server.

bump.desc: Raise the version in package.json; does not commit, tag or edit CHANGELOG.md
bump.detail: Prints the next steps: add the CHANGELOG.md section, commit, then `just release tag`. Undo with `git checkout package.json`.

args.name: <level>
args.desc: Which part of the version to raise

contents.desc: List the files the npm tarball would contain, without writing it
contents.detail: Use it after changing the files list in package.json.

publish.desc: Publish to npm under the beta dist-tag after the acceptance test; extra args go to npm publish
publish.detail: Runs `just release accept` first and asks before it publishes. Uses the npm login on this machine (`npm login`); never pass a token as an argument. A published version cannot be reused, even after `npm unpublish`.

args.name: [npm-publish-args...]
args.desc: Forwarded to npm publish, such as --dry-run or --otp <code>

tag.desc: Create the local git tag v<version> from package.json; refuses on a dirty tree; does not push
tag.detail: Also refuses when the tag exists or when CHANGELOG.md has no section for the version. Undo by deleting the local tag with git. Push with `git push origin v<version>`.

exits.1: dirty tree, tag exists, or no CHANGELOG.md section

examples.desc: Show what npm would publish, without publishing

sample.label: Tasks and Pokemon sample APIs on port 3000

install.desc: Install the npm dependencies of one sample API (npm ci)
install.detail: Optional: serve and test install the dependencies on first use.

serve.desc: Serve one sample API in the foreground on port 3000; Ctrl-C stops it
serve.detail: Then run its manifest from another terminal: `just run api-samples/tasks/api-tests.json` or `just run api-samples/pokemon/tram.json`.

stop.desc: Kill every process that listens on port 3000, sample API or not
stop.detail: Prints each process before it sends SIGTERM, and asks first. Use it when a sample recipe reports that port 3000 is in use.

test.desc: Start a sample API, run its manifest, save the report and transcript under .tram/
test.detail: Writes .tram/<name>/report.json and .tram/<name>/transcript.http, overwriting the last run, and stops the server afterwards. Fails at once when port 3000 is in use. `just ci` runs the stricter test/tasks-integration.js instead, which also checks the expected counts.

exits.1: a test failed, or the server did not start

examples.desc: Serve the Tasks API for manual runs with just run
Run the Pokemon manifest and keep the evidence in .tram/pokemon/

sample.footer: Both sample APIs listen on port 3000, so only one runs at a time.

deploy.desc: Start the GitHub Pages workflow that publishes site/ from main
deploy.detail: Publishes what is on origin/main, not your working tree. A push to main that changes site/ starts the same workflow by itself. Needs `gh auth login`.

serve.desc: Serve site/ at http://localhost:8080 for a local preview
